findings.issue: Client-side multi-column sorting with direction toggle, numeric/string compare, and missing-values-last-in-both-directions is untested; this is the most intricate comparator in the app.
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests for the sort (extract it to a .svelte.ts module): nulls last ascending and descending, direction flip, tie-break by name, aria-sort state per column.

findings.issue: URL state (q/type/generation/page) with validation, 48-per-page slicing, page clamping to pageCount, and default-omission is untested; a refactor of the data layer could silently break edge pages or invalid params.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the load against a stubbed api module: empty/garbage page param, page beyond last, invalid type/generation names, combined filters, count text.

findings.issue: pokemonCards' alternate-form exclusion (`id <= MAX_DEFAULT_ID`) and dedupe are untested; flipping the comparison or mishandling NaN from idFromUrl (app/src/lib/server/api.ts:57-59) would leak Mega forms into every list or drop valid Pokémon.
findings.suggestion: Test pokemonCards with mixed IDs including >10000, duplicates, and a non-matching URL; assert ordering and species-name resolution.

findings.issue: Moves pipeline is untested: version-group ordering by `order`, default game selection (highest order), method table ordering (level-up/machine/egg/tutor then alphabetical), and the dedup key `${method}|${move}|${level}` that intentionally keeps same move at different levels but must not duplicate machine moves.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with a synthetic pokemon payload covering a move learned at two levels and via two methods; assert table membership, order, and row keys.

findings.issue: The 60s promise cache is untested: 404-null caching, eviction of rejected promises only while still current, and unbounded growth of successful entries (no eviction besides TTL expiry checks) are all easy to break in a refactor.
findings.suggestion: Test get() with a mocked fetch: 404 → null, shared promise for concurrent calls, failed request not cached, expired entry refetched.

findings.issue: The search box's race handling (150ms debounce, `replace` navigation, `afterNavigate` only syncing q on non-goto navigations) is subtle client state-vs-URL logic with no tests; stale keystrokes overwriting results or lost state on back/forward would slip through.
findings.suggestion: Add a component/E2E test: type two characters quickly and assert the final URL and rendered list reflect the last query; test back/forward restores the input value.

findings.issue: Type index construction (slot ordering per Pokémon, filtering stellar/unknown/shadow) and generation species sets are untested; mis-sorted slots would render wrong type badges everywhere with nothing failing.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test getTypes/getGenerations against fixture payloads with out-of-order slots and the excluded type names.

findings.issue: Recursive evolutionTree and the fallback when a species has no evolution_chain URL are untested; malformed chains (null evolves_to) would throw a 500.
findings.suggestion: Test evolutionTree with branching (Eevee-like) and empty chains.

findings.issue: 404-vs-500 branching and title formatting are untested; a regression would show 'Something went wrong' for missing Pokémon.
findings.suggestion: Cover with a routing test hitting /pokemon/missingno and an erroring route.

findings.issue: Pure spec-critical helpers (humanize, dexNumber padding, display em-dash) are trivial to test and easy to accidentally regress (e.g. '#25' vs '#0025'); they're free wins the author left on the table.
findings.suggestion: A five-line vitest file covering humanize('mr-mime'), dexNumber(25), display(null) would cost nothing and guard the most-reused code.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own — no runner, no script, no test files — while carrying a meaningful amount of high-risk logic: client-side table sorting, URL-driven filtering and pagination, alternate-form exclusion, and a TTL request cache. A refactor of the data layer would be entirely unguarded once the acceptance suite stops being the safety net. The code is reasonably factored (pure helpers, thin loads), so adding tests would be cheap; it just wasn't done.
